title: LLM Evaluation, Observability & Guardrails: Eval Sets, Judges & Prompt Injection
concept: Ship LLM features you can measure and defend: representative eval sets, automatic checks and LLM-as-judge checked against people, regression gates in CI, traces of every model call, PII redaction, and defences against prompt injection and unsafe output handling.
description: An advanced course for engineers who run an LLM feature in production. Every lesson starts from an incident on the CodeDev learning platform's AI grading assistant - a student submission that told the model to give full marks, a score from the model written straight into the database, an AI-written feedback panel that rendered the model's HTML, a prompt change that looked better on five examples and worse on five hundred, learner emails in the trace logs - and fixes it with a check you can automate: eval sets, eval runners, judge-human agreement with Cohen's kappa, regression gates with a minimum sample size, tracing token, latency and cost, PII redaction, detecting leaked solutions, separating data from instructions, validating model output, and safe rendering. 12 lessons with True/False quizzes on real prompts, traces and outputs, and TypeScript challenges graded by hidden tests on recorded outputs.

learningOutcomes.text: Build representative eval sets and run automatic checks on recorded outputs
Use LLM-as-judge only with measured agreement against human graders
Gate prompt and model changes in CI with a regression threshold and a minimum sample
Trace LLM calls with tokens, latency, model and cost, and redact personal data
Defend against prompt injection, unvalidated output and unsafe rendering

knownIssues: No real model is called: challenges use recorded outputs and fake judges
